high_level_description: Wordless hand-colored French Renaissance woodcut book illustration of a busy Parisian printer-bookseller's workshop, where one olive-marked edition leaves the same press as several identical copies carried toward a school, a library, and the street market, while every exemplar preserves the originating workshop's device.

compositional_deconstruction.background: An open-fronted Parisian printshop from the 1540s occupies the upper half of a narrow cobbled street, with pale limestone walls, dark oak beams, a small-paned rear window, and a college doorway across the lane. A recessed library entrance stands farther right in natural daylight. No signboard, inscription, letter, numeral, arrow, diagram, royal emblem, ownership stamp, nor halo appears anywhere. No modern object appears.

elements.desc: Oak screw printing press, large and left of center, fitted with a black inked forme whose sole image is a branching olive tree inside a plain oval. The platen is raised above one damp sheet. Its frame, bar, tympan, frisket, and inked bed follow a sixteenth-century hand press, with neither modern controls nor written labels.

Master printer operating the press, light-brown skin, short dark beard, black flat cap, indigo wool doublet, ivory linen shirt, brown hose, leather apron, and brown shoes. His focused gaze follows the platen while both hands draw the wooden bar. His clothing and hands show no crown, seal, badge, key, recipient document, nor institutional object.

Wooden drying rack carrying four freshly printed title sheets from the same forme, arranged at different heights without numbering. Every sheet is otherwise blank and bears one identical black olive-tree device in the same central position, with matching branches, oval boundary, and small exposed roots. No receiving institution adds another mark.

Traveling book carrier leaving the workshop, medium-brown skin, curly black hair beneath a rust wool cap, ochre tunic, blue knee-length cloak, brown hose, and sturdy leather shoes. He walks toward the street market with two wicker panniers of bound copies; the uppermost open volume displays the same olive-tree device and no other symbol.

Young university reader beside the college doorway, fair skin, straight chestnut hair under a black scholar's cap, dark green gown, ivory collar, brown hose, and black shoes. He studies one purchased open volume whose otherwise blank title page carries the same olive-tree device, while the press and its operators remain visibly separate behind him.

Library porter approaching the recessed entrance, dark-brown skin, close-cropped black hair, plain blue cap, muted red knee-length coat, cream shirt, charcoal hose, and brown shoes. He supports a stack of unbound folded quires; the visible top sheet bears the same olive-tree device. It has no library stamp, new signature, altered branch, and no added decoration.
